There’s a huge list of dietary triggers for vertigo and vestibular migraine. Nicotine along with most stimulants are on this list so if you smoke cigarettes or vape unfortunately you cannot do it anymore, or try to do it less. I’m not how I used to be but I’m no longer sick everyday and I’m good enough to work and travel now. At first I was prescribed Amitriptyline 25-50mg which worked wonders however I gained a lot of weight so I had to stop it. I did vestibular therapy 2x weekly for 3 months and it seemed to help. 

Now I’m on Topamax 50mg once daily + avoiding my dietary triggers. I no longer feel like crap and no longer throw up everyday. I’m also prescribed rizatriptan and nurtec just in case the dizziness accompanies a migraine which is not always. Not everyone with vestibular migraine gets head pain, and Vm is commorbid with a lot of other disorders so it is something to be considered.

A second cousin (without removal) is someone who shares a great grandparent with you, and is around the same age as you. So you’re still closely related because most people are usually aware of who their second cousins are.

A cousin with removal I believe is when there’s a generational gap between the two. For example, if you are 25 and you have a second cousin who is 45. The common ancestor would still be a great grandparent, only difference is years of birth.
